question: As per NITI Aayog National Multidimensional Poverty Index – 2021, which state is the poorest?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Bihar**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Bihar** is identified as the** poorest state** according to the **NITI Aayog National Multidimensional Poverty Index – 2021**.
 
• The Multidimensional Poverty Index (MPI) takes into account various factors such as health, education, and standard of living to** measure poverty beyond income levels**.
 
• Bihar has the highest percentage of its population living in multidimensional poverty, making it the poorest state as per the 2021 index.
 
• Other states with significant levels of poverty include Jharkhand and Uttar Pradesh, but Bihar leads the list.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **NITI Aayog** is a policy think tank of the Government of India, established with the aim to achieve sustainable development goals and to enhance cooperative federalism by fostering the involvement of State Governments in the economic policy-making process.
 
• The **National Multidimensional Poverty Index** is part of the global effort to measure poverty in a more comprehensive manner, reflecting the multiple deprivations that people face in their daily lives.
 
• The index is aligned with the global MPI developed by the United Nations Development Programme (UNDP) and the Oxford Poverty and Human Development Initiative (OPHI).
 
• The aim of the MPI is to provide a more nuanced understanding of poverty and to guide policy interventions for poverty alleviation.
